title: Review: planning an outing
why: This review closes unit 3 by putting all its irregular verbs to work in one situation: proposing, accepting and turning down an outing. You'll combine vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, connaître and the verbs of movement to plan a Saturday in Marseille.

Proposing an outing

This review lesson adds no new grammar: it brings together the verbs of unit 3 for a very real situation, planning an outing with friends. First, the verbs you need, at a glance:

jenousils, elles
allervaisallonsvont
venirviensvenonsviennent
sortirsorssortonssortent
fairefaisfaisonsfont
vouloirveuxvoulonsveulent
pouvoirpeuxpouvonspeuvent
devoirdoisdevonsdoivent
savoirsaissavonssavent
connaîtreconnaisconnaissonsconnaissent
préférerpréfèrepréféronspréfèrent

How to propose

  • Tu veux sortir ce soir ? / Vous voulez venir samedi ?: with vouloir.
  • On va au cinéma ?: with on and rising intonation, the most common way among friends.
  • Tu es libre samedi ?: to check first.
  • Ça te dit ?: “How about it? Do you feel like it?” Take it as a fixed phrase (te is a pronoun you'll study later).
Il fait beau samedi : on va à la plage ? Ça te dit ?The weather's nice on Saturday: shall we go to the beach? How about it?

French uses the present for plans: Samedi, on va à la plage = On Saturday, we're going to the beach. No future tense needed.

", "

Saying yes, saying no

FrenchEnglish
Avec plaisir !With pleasure! I'd love to!
Bonne idée !Good idea!
D'accord !OK! All right!
Pourquoi pas ?Why not?
Désolé, je ne peux pas.Sorry, I can't.
Je dois travailler.I have to work.
Je préfère rester à la maison.I'd rather stay at home.

A good refusal gives a reason, usually with devoir, and if possible a counter-proposal, with préférer or pouvoir:

Désolée, samedi, je ne peux pas : je dois travailler. Mais dimanche, je peux !Sorry, I can't on Saturday: I have to work. But on Sunday I can!
La plage ? Je préfère la randonnée : je ne sais pas nager !The beach? I'd rather go hiking: I can't swim!

Checking the details

Before you go, use savoir for information and connaître for places:

Tu connais la calanque de Sugiton ? Tu sais à quelle heure part le bus ?Do you know the Sugiton cove? Do you know what time the bus leaves?

Keep the two “can'ts” apart: je ne sais pas nager (I can't swim: a skill) vs je ne peux pas venir (I can't come: I'm not available).

", "

Getting organized

Once everyone agrees, you settle the time, the meeting point and the transport. All of this works in the present.

FrenchEnglish
On part à quelle heure ?What time are we leaving?
Rendez-vous à neuf heures au Vieux-Port.Let's meet at nine at the Old Port.
On va à la calanque en bus ?Shall we go to the cove by bus?
Il faut marcher une heure.You have to walk for an hour.
Je prends le maillot de bain et la crème solaire.I'm bringing my swimsuit and the sunscreen.
Il fait chaud : tu mets un chapeau !It's hot: put on a hat!
On se retrouve au restaurant.We'll meet up at the restaurant.

Marseille is the perfect setting: les calanques are rocky coves between Marseille and Cassis that you reach on foot or by boat, and le Vieux-Port (the Old Port) is the heart of the city.

Rendez-vous with a time and a place means “Let's meet…”: Rendez-vous à huit heures à la gare ! In English the word sounds romantic or secretive; in French it's an everyday word for any meeting or appointment, even with the dentist.
